title: session_bus.v1
description: Session-bus message and queue-row schemas (M1). Validated by scripts/coordination/session_bus.py. Owning handoff: handoffs/active/session-bus-thin-dispatcher.md. Single-writer ownership is a protocol property enforced by the CLI's `validate` lint, NOT by this schema, so writer violations report distinctly from structural failures.

id.description: msg-<compact-utc>-<seq>-<writer>, e.g. msg-20260727T182214Z-1-claude-main. Lexicographically sortable; deliberately free of offset punctuation so the id is a single clean token.

corr_ids.description: C23 (2026-08-11): every routed message this ONE row dispositions, in addition to any scalar `corr_id`. Added because the previous rule was not performable: clearing triage took one corr_id per item, so a session holding a single answer for N routed items had no compliant way to send it once, and BUS_PROTOCOL.md told authors to 'write it once and reference it' while no mechanism to reference it existed. Measured 2026-07-29: 9 byte-identical payloads in 10 minutes from one careful main, hours after that discipline rule was codified — and fan-out makes it N dispositions x M routing targets. Purely additive: the scalar still works and is still right for a genuinely per-item answer. Use this ONLY when one answer really does cover every id listed; N distinct answers still want N rows, because a reader who cannot tell N answers from one answer repeated N times has lost the signal the queue exists to carry.

operator_signature_needed.description: C49 (2026-08-12): author-set POSITIVE marker — true means this message needs A HUMAN'S signature, not a named agent's action. Deliberately declared here at the generic `payload` level, not inside a per-kind `allOf` branch, because it is legal on ANY kind, not one. Replaces an INFERRED predicate (`kind in {token-request, defect}` OR `severity`/`priority == CRITICAL`) measured 2026-08-12 against 267 live inbox rows: 116 carried `action_required` (agent-action, never operator), only 8 satisfied the old predicate, and just 7 overlapped — near-disjoint in both directions. Every one of those 8 was `kind: defect` (fleet-internal engineering work); not one was a `token-request`, the only kind that IS an operator gate by definition. `_is_operator_item` (scripts/coordination/session_bus_coordinator.py) is now `payload.operator_signature_needed is True` OR `kind == 'token-request'` — token-request stays because a token IS the operator's signature, and dropping it would silence that channel. Absent or false is the default: `action_required`/`needs_routing_to` route to a named agent, never the operator, and CRITICAL severity does not imply operator-ness either.

relayed_src.description: Set by the coordinator-daemon when it relays an agent-authored outbox message into a recipient inbox: the source msg id. Carries the dedupe key so relay is idempotent across ticks (defect C2, 2026-07-28). Absent on daemon-generated messages.

_renamed_from.description: Migration provenance: the roster id this row was authored under, before the 2026-07-29 rename (claude-gpu-lane / claude-main / fable-auditor / codex -> the current ids). Written by the rename migration onto the 217 rows it rewrote, so `from`/`to` could be updated without losing who actually sent the message. PERMITTED 2026-08-11 (C34, second half): the migration wrote it, `additionalProperties: false` forbade it, and the relay therefore refused all 217 rows — including five operator token-requests stranded for two weeks. Stripping it was the alternative and is not available: an outbox has exactly one writer and it is not the daemon, so the choice was to accept the provenance or lose the mail. Historical only; nothing should write this field again.
_renamed_from.$comment: Underscore-prefixed by convention: tool-written provenance, not agent-authored content.

needs_routing_to.description: STRUCTURAL routing intent (2026-07-29): the roster ids this message must REACH, beyond the transport `to`. Added because two routed messages were missed when routing intent lived as prose inside `payload` and a context-economy truncation cut exactly the sentence carrying it. Prose is not a routing channel: tools act on this field. Entries must be roster ids (append refuses unknowns). A message with this field appears in each named agent's `triage` standing queue until that agent dispositions it by corr_id from its own outbox — advancing a cursor never clears it.

action_required.description: STRUCTURAL action intent (2026-07-29): the routed-to agents (needs_routing_to, else a concrete `to`) must ACT, not merely receive. Stays in their `triage` queue until dispositioned by an outbox row with matching corr_id that is either a substantive kind (anything but a bare ack) or an ack with payload.disposition in {done, declined, handed-off, superseded}. A bare ack marks it acked-but-unactioned and it KEEPS appearing: acknowledgment is receipt, not action. `append` refuses action_required on to='*' with needs_routing_to unset — intent with no addressee is the failure shape this field exists to kill.

payload.description: Pre-validation is MANDATORY: an operator command that fails is a defect row attributed to the requesting agent.

R4 — request that a holder give its lease back. Authority is checked against config.yaml authority.lease_grant; an unauthorised sender is rejected with a defect row. Revocation is ALWAYS quiesce-and-drain at the holder's next boundary (fabric axiom 4) — never a kill.

yield_to.description: task_id or priority class this yields to

payload.description: How work ENTERS the queue. Agents never write queue.jsonl — they propose, and the coordinator-daemon transcribes (pure bookkeeping, no judgment). gating is mandatory here for the same reason it is mandatory on the row: without it a lease revocation has no defined fallback set.

spec_ref.description: owning handoff (+ checkbox anchor) — the spec stays OUT of the row

classification.description: how lane/gating were decided — 'heuristic' means provisional

queue_row.title: session_bus.queue.v1
queue_row.description: Appended by the coordinator-daemon ONLY. Fold is latest-row-per-task_id-wins (batch_ledger.reconcile semantics). Agents propose and report; they never write this file.

gating.description: R4 prerequisite — REQUIRED. Without it a lease revocation has no defined fallback set and the keep-working rule cannot be honoured.

contention_class.description: R5 pausability. exclusive-contiguous = decision-gating timing run, never paused.

spec_ref.description: spec stays OUT of the row

replay_eligible.description: R9 — result obtainable by deterministic replay over banked outputs: needs no lane, no claim, no token.

role_affinity.description: R3 — the stack role whose resource profile this task resembles, used to look the task up in the MEASURED contention matrix (per-role-pair verdicts). Distinct from contention_class, which is the pausability axis. Absent means co-residency is not applicable to this task, not that it is permitted.

revoking.description: R4 — the coordinator-agent has asked for this lease back. The task keeps its current status because it IS still running; the holder stops accepting new work and releases at its next boundary (axiom 4). A revoking task is never re-assigned while still held.
